transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-23 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood CSM), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Sofia Alvarez (Redwood TPM); Priya Nair (Argosware Head ML), Carlos Mendes (Argosware VP Eng), Ethan Shaw (Argosware Security), Nina Patel (Argosware Platform)

Summary:
Redwood CSM kickoff for final pre-go-live readiness. Main topics: security/compliance (SOC2, KMS, SSO), network (VPC peering, egress), performance (latency SLOs, dedicated vs hosted), cost considerations (batching/quantization), rollout plan and concrete next steps.

Topics:
- Security artifacts and KMS integration
- Network/topology and VPC peering
- Performance benchmarks and expected SLAs
- Data residency and retention settings
- Pilot -> canary -> prod rollout schedule
Action items (brief in-meeting list): Maya to send docs; Liam to run bench; customer to send traffic sample.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for making time, i know it's a busy week so we'll try to get through the checklist quickly. this is the pre-go-live readiness check, want to make sure security, networking, and perf all aligned.
[00:18] Priya Nair: thanks maya. quick note, we're aiming for a soft launch next tuesday, so anything blocking we need to get moved this week.
[00:26] Carlos Mendes: yes we're on a tight window, engineering has a code freeze friday.
[00:32] Maya Chen: got it. rough plan for today: review the outstanding security docs, confirm VPC peering steps and egress routing, go over the benchmark plan liam has, and then close on next steps. liam do you want to lead perf?
[00:44] Liam O'Connor: sure, yes. quick heads up, we prepared two bench profiles — a 1000-query low-latency profile and a sustained QPS profile to emulate peak. we can run both on hosted and dedicated variants. note: "dedicated" here means reserved capacity with pinned GPU pools — not just larger shared instances. not to confuse with on-prem.
[01:10] Priya Nair: good. latency target we discussed earlier is p95 < 250ms for short prompts (~200 tokens). is that still realistic on hosted?
[01:22] Liam O'Connor: for short prompts yes on hosted with our latency-first routing it is realistic for many open models we curate. for bulk throughput the dedicated pool gives more predictable p95 under sustained load. there is a tradeoff: dedicated reduces variance but costs more at low util.
[01:42] Ethan Shaw: can i jump in — on security we need to verify SOC 2 status, encryption at rest/in transit, KMS integration, and also audit log retention. what's your retention granularity for logs and do you redact tokens?
[01:56] Maya Chen: good q. we are SOC 2 Type II, i'll send the report. on logs, we have optional request/response audit trail; default hosted retains a short window but we can export logs to customer S3 for longer retention. token-level redaction is configurable — we can mask PII before persisting. i'll attach the architecture diagram.
[02:20] Ethan Shaw: and KMS — do you support customer-managed keys/hsm? rotation policies?
[02:27] Sofia Alvarez: yes, we support KMS integrations for private deployments and for our Private offering we can integrate customer KMS (cloud KMS or HSM). for hosted we offer envelope encryption and can support BYOK (bring your own key) for enterprise agreements. rotation policy is configurable, we'll share options.
[02:45] Nina Patel: subtle point on network: our infra team prefers VPC peering over public egress, we also have strict egress rules. what ports/ip ranges do you need?
[02:56] Liam O'Connor: we'll provide a minimal set — typically https outbound to our control plane and grpc endpoints to the inference cluster IP ranges. i'll put the CIDR ranges and example peering steps in the diagram. note sometimes peering requires route table adjustments for long haul.
[03:18] Carlos Mendes: regarding data residency — our EU customers must keep training data in eu-west region, how do you handle region pinning?
[03:27] Maya Chen: we have region affinity routing: you can pin requests to a region or a private deployment. for hosted, we have eu regions and can enforce routing policies. also for Private deployments you get full regional control.
[03:40] Priya Nair: okay on perf, liam said he'd run two benches. what's the sample dataset you need from us?
[03:49] Liam O'Connor: ideally a CSV with average tokens per request, distribution (short/medium/long), and a small set of representative prompts (20-50) so we can measure p50/p95/p99 and cost per 1k tokens. if you can include the QPS target that helps.
[04:10] Nina Patel: we'll export a sample. one extra ask: can redwood support prefix caching for repeated system prompts? that's key for us cause we send the same system instructions a lot.
[04:21] Liam O'Connor: yes, we have automatic prefix/KV caching that should reduce cost and latency for repeated prefixes. we can enable it per route, and tune TTLs. there might be edge cases with stateful convo caches but we can test with your prompts.
[04:39] Ethan Shaw: SSO/IDP — do you integrate with our SAML provider? also RBAC — need admin/ops/service account separation and token rotation.
[04:50] Sofia Alvarez: we integrate SAML/SSO for the console and RBAC with roles (admin/operator/viewer). for API keys we support short-lived tokens and can integrate with OIDC/SAML for service accounts via our private connector. i'll attach the RBAC table.
[05:08] Priya Nair: on the rollout plan — we want a pilot with ~500 daily users for a week, then a canary with 10% traffic for 48 hours, then 100% roll. does that align with your recommended flow?
[05:17] Maya Chen: yes that's our standard cadence: pilot -> canary -> ramp. for canary we recommend traffic splitting at the load balancer and automatic fallback to a stable model variant in case of regression. we'll provide the canary playbook.
[05:33] Carlos Mendes: cost — can you ballpark cost differences between hosted and dedicated for our profile? we care about 99th percentile spikes during business hours.
[05:44] Liam O'Connor: rough back-of-envelope: for low to moderate steady usage hosted tends to be cheaper because you avoid underutilized reserved GPUs. but at sustained high QPS dedicated amortizes better. quantization and batching can cut per-token cost 30-50% depending on model. i'll run numbers once i have your token distribution.
[06:05] Priya Nair: quick question — do you support mixed-model fallbacks (e.g., if the large LLM is busy, route to a smaller quantized model)?
[06:13] Liam O'Connor: yes, smart routing supports model variants and automatic fallback policies; we can route by latency or cost thresholds. we also support automatic downgrade to cached completions for specific routes.
[06:27] Ethan Shaw: on compliance docs — besides SOC2, do you have ISO or FedRAMP artifacts? some of our partners may ask.
[06:36] Maya Chen: we are SOC2 Type II today; ISO is in the roadmap. for FedRAMP we don't currently hold authority but we can discuss private deployment and on-premise packages for highly regulated partners.
[06:50] Nina Patel: what's the typical SLA for Dedicated?
[06:55] Sofia Alvarez: Dedicated customers get an SLA on uptime and latency targets associated with the pool size; we'll share the SLA doc. for onboarding customers we typically commit to 99.9% availability with burst capacity options.
[07:10] Priya Nair: ok great. any blockers you see from your side?
[07:14] Liam O'Connor: just the sample traffic and a quick VPC peering window to validate network paths. and access to a staging API key for the bench.
[07:25] Maya Chen: action items recap — i'll send SOC2 and network diagram, liam will run bench, nina will share traffic; we schedule a network walkthrough.
[07:36] Carlos Mendes: one last technical nit — do you support proactive KV cache invalidation? sometimes we push updated system prompts and want caches to flush.
[07:47] Liam O'Connor: yes we do provide a cache invalidation API and TTL controls per route. not all caches are global immediate but we can force a flush on deploy hooks.
[07:59] Priya Nair: thanks everyone. shall we aim to reconvene after the bench results next friday?
[08:05] Maya Chen: sounds good. i'll coordinate the calendar. thanks all.

End of transcript.

Notes: occasional transcription artifacts ("HSM" heard as "H-S-M", "CIDR" sometimes typed as "sider"). References: link to SOC2 report (placeholder), network diagram (placeholder), bench spreadsheet (placeholder).
